headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while the weekly tape and the ETF desk both lean the other way
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB and XRP are all above their 200-day averages with golden crosses confirmed on the first four. DOGE and ADA are the exceptions, both below trend with no golden cross. Seven assets, five in an established uptrend by this measure, two not. That's a market where the primary trend still points up for the majors even as the last week has been rough.

And the last week has been rough, which is the divergence worth naming. BTC is up 0.6% on the day but down 5.3% on the week, up 18.7% on the month. ETH: up 0.7% today, down 4.0% on the week, up 29.2% on the month. SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA all show the identical pattern, small green days sitting inside red weeks sitting inside green months. RSI readings cluster near neutral (BTC 49.8, ETH 51.6, SOL 51.0, XRP 46.5), and MACD is below signal across the board. That combination, flat momentum with negative MACD crosses inside an intact 200-day uptrend, reads as a market resting or mildly correcting after its monthly advance, not one accelerating. The month's strength hasn't been erased, but the week's pullback has drained the momentum gauges back to the middle of the range.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0087% per 8 hours (9.5% annualized), modest but positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade, a normal cost in an uptrend, not an overheated one. Open interest is $2.15B on BTC with a long/short account ratio of 1.73, and ETH's ratio runs even richer at 2.12, XRP at 3.14, DOGE at 4.7. Longs dominate the account count across the board. The liquidation windows show the tape enforcing that lean: BTC's 4-hour window saw $501,531 in long liquidations against $145,517 in shorts, ETH's 2-hour window saw shorts take the bigger hit ($211,139 vs $67,357 in longs), and XRP's 5-hour window shows a lopsided $1.75M in short liquidations against $212,250 in longs, likely squeezed by the day's 1.1% bounce. Crowded long positioning paying modest funding is not fragile in the way expensive, one-sided funding would be, but it's also not neutral.

Flows are where the real tension sits. BTC spot ETFs printed a net outflow of $102.6M on 16 Sep 2026, and the five-session net is a larger outflow of $689.0M, same direction both windows, so this one doesn't need hedging: the traditional-finance bid has been net negative lately. ETH ETFs disagree with themselves: a $13.9M outflow on the day sits against a $151.4M net inflow over five sessions, a genuine window conflict worth flagging rather than smoothing over. Whale wallets, meanwhile, moved $171.4M net off exchanges in the last 24 hours (BTC contributing $160.9M of that, ETH $10.5M), continuing a weekly pattern: the past four tracked weeks show onto-exchange weeks (Aug 26: $1,580M onto exchanges; Sep 09: $536M onto exchanges; the week ending Sep 16: $593M onto exchanges) bracketing one off-exchange week (Sep 02: $371M off). So the most recent 24 hours point off-exchange even as the broader weekly trend has leaned onto-exchange three of the last four prints, another disagreement across windows that's worth sitting with rather than resolving.

Sentiment is the calmest read of the day: Fear & Greed sits at 51, dead neutral, near the low end of its own 30-day range of 41 to 74. The crowd isn't panicking and isn't euphoric, it's shrugging, which is a reasonable response to a tape that's up on the day, down on the week, up on the month, with a positioning book still tilted long and an ETF desk pulling BTC money out while whale wallets pull BTC coins off exchanges. Total market cap is down 1.95% over 24 hours to $2.61T, BTC dominance holds at 58.4%, and stablecoin float has grown a modest 1.1% over 30 days to $309.5B, dry powder present but not surging.

Worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF outflow extends or reverses, whether the whale weekly figure flips back to onto-exchange the way three of the last four weeks have run, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on BTC or ETH, which would mark the current rest phase turning back into acceleration rather than continuing to cool.
